testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you have more than one license:

options.text: You probably won't get caught.
You should keep it secret.
States can find out through a shared computer system.

questions.correctAnswerText: States can find out through a shared computer system.
questions.explanation: All states share driver information through a computer database to prevent one person from getting multiple licenses. Having more than one driver license is illegal.

questions.question: Texting while driving is:

options.text: Allowed if you are contacting your employer.
Allowed on rural roads.
Not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and never permitted while operating a vehicle.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest driving speed is:

options.text: Slower than other vehicles around you.
The same speed as other vehicles around you.
Faster than other vehicles around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as other vehicles around you.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, it is safest to travel at the same speed as other vehicles. If two vehicles move in the same direction at the same speed, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Do not have to do anything related to crossings.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the proper way to cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign to shift to a higher gear?

options.text: Road speed
Engine RPMs
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear. First is engine speed (RPM). Read your vehicle's manual to learn the RPM range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (MPH). Learn which speeds work for each gear, watch your speedometer, and shift up as needed.

questions.question: When you start an engine, oil pressure should reach normal level:

options.text: Within seconds.
Within five minutes.
After about three minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Watch your truck's gauges when starting the engine. Oil pressure should reach a normal level within seconds after the engine starts.

questions.question: When making a tight turn, a vehicle operator should:

options.text: Drive as fast as a regular car.
Not worry about speed and just focus on the road.
Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake early and slow down gradually to warn drivers behind.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not expect how slowly your vehicle must go to safely make a tight turn. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them in advance.

questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs are:

options.text: Safe if a professional did the repairs.
Safe if the repair looks solid.
Not safe to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not safe to use.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe. They must be replaced before the vehicle can be driven.

questions.question: ____ are most affected by strong winds.

options.text: Light vehicles
Heavy vehicles
Vehicles with open windows

questions.correctAnswerText: Light vehicles
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to control your vehicle. This is especially true for drivers of lighter vehicles.

questions.question: The only way to sober up after drinking alcohol is to:

options.text: Take a cold shower.
Exercise.
Wait.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate. Cold showers and black coffee do not speed this up. The only way to become sober is to give your body time to process the alcohol.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving skills test, what vehicle must you use?

options.text: You can use any vehicle.
You must use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
The vehicle type does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
questions.explanation: You must take the skills test in the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.

questions.question: How should cargo inside a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no more than three feet high.
It should be secured to keep it from moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured to keep it from moving.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured to prevent it from shifting during transport.

questions.question: Vehicle inspections are required by whom?

options.text: Most employers
Insurance companies
State and federal law

questions.correctAnswerText: State and federal law
questions.explanation: Federal and state law require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip.

questions.question: Which item is an example of required emergency equipment?

options.text: A spare electrical fuse
A loud horn
A battery-operated flashlight

questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: How do you know if a vehicle can handle a load?

options.text: Know the vehicle's suspension rating.
Know the tire rating for the front tires only.
Start driving and see how the vehicle handles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know the vehicle's suspension rating.
questions.explanation: You must know the vehicle's weight capacity and suspension rating to make sure it is not overloaded.

questions.question: When backing, what should you do?

options.text: Move quickly to get out of other drivers' ways.
Try not to use the mirrors.
Use a helper, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper, if possible.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Use a helper to watch your blind spots whenever you can.

questions.question: How should air tank drains be used?

options.text: The driver should not use them.
Only use them when it is wet outside.
Use them to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use them to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Air in the brake system contains water and oil. These build up and can damage the brakes. Open air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When should you shift into a lower gear before going downhill?

options.text: As you begin to move downward
As you go downhill and pick up speed
Before you start going downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start going downhill
questions.explanation: Slow down and shift to a lower gear before you start going downhill. If you don't, your brakes may overheat and fail.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: It tells the motor carrier about problems that may need fixing.
It ensures that the vehicle is inspected regularly.
It holds drivers accountable for inspecting the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells the motor carrier about problems that may need fixing.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report informs the motor carrier of any safety problems. The carrier must repair these items or report that repairs were not needed.

questions.question: How do you use the controlled braking method?

options.text: Lock your wheels while braking.
Apply your brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply your brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Make very small steering movements when using this method.

questions.question: What is aggressive driving?

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
Driving with care for other drivers' safety.
Driving in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy way without regard for the rights or safety of other drivers.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, how often must you check that it is secure?

options.text: Every 10 miles.
Every 150 miles.
Every 500 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo security before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down all the way and release. If it does not return to normal, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down all the way and release. If it squeaks, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times and then press hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or other brake system problem.

questions.question: What makes up the emergency brake system?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system.
Only parts of the service brake system.
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three braking systems: service, parking, and emergency. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Prevent your wheels from locking up.
Lock up your vehicle's wheels.
Stop your vehicle from accelerating uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: When you pull over to the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on your taillights to warn other drivers.
Do not worry about other drivers.
Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road, especially when visibility is low. Place warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: What can a broken exhaust system do?

options.text: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab.
Improve fuel efficiency.
Make steering harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous because poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Drive on the shoulder.
Let the vehicle pass you.
Drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the vehicle pass you.
questions.explanation: If someone is following too closely, give them space to pass safely. Driving faster is not safe because the other driver may continue tailgating you at the higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to finish your trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Safely pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy, stop and sleep. Tired drivers cause many fatal accidents. Do not try to push through and finish your trip.

questions.question: What information must interstate carriers display on their commercial vehicles?

options.text: Business name.
Width of the truck.
Length of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Business name.
questions.explanation: Federal rules require carriers to display the legal name or business name on each commercial vehicle in their fleet.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They store compressed air for the brakes.
They should be drained of air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They store compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air that the brakes use. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: You must tell your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation, regardless of what vehicle you were driving. Parking violations are the only exception.

questions.question: When alley docking, what should you do first?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop your vehicle parallel to the outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space.

questions.question: What is true about Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?

options.text: They reduce a vehicle's braking power.
They work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
They do not work well on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works with your normal brakes and does not change your braking power. ABS only activates when your wheels are about to lock up.

questions.question: How often must you check that cargo is secure?

options.text: Every 10 miles.
Every 150 miles.
Every 500 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement within the first 50 miles of your trip. Then check it again every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.question: What can affect stopping distance?

options.text: Driving speed.
Temperature.
Time of day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving speed.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is affected by your vehicle's speed, its weight, and how much grip the road surface provides.

questions.question: How far ahead should you scan the road?

options.text: Two to three seconds ahead.
Five to six seconds ahead.
12 to 15 seconds ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 seconds ahead.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards and react to them. Look for vehicles entering the highway or changing into your lane.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire missing one or two lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring is safe if you drive under 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lug nuts are dangerous. Do not drive with mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings. Check your tires and rims before driving your commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What prevents wheel lockup when braking?

options.text: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).
Air brakes.
An alternator.

questions.correctAnswerText: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking up while you are braking.

questions.question: What is true about driving in hot weather?

options.text: Air pressure in tires will decrease.
Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
Antifreeze is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine oil helps keep the engine cool.
questions.explanation: In hot weather, air pressure in tires increases. Your engine needs enough oil and coolant to stay cool. Antifreeze is important in both hot and cold weather.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of retarder?

options.text: Exhaust
Engine
Air

questions.correctAnswerText: Air
questions.explanation: Retarders are devices that help slow a vehicle and reduce brake wear. The four basic types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric retarders.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:

options.text: Every three hours.
Every day.
Every other week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every day.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from forming in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Be done the same way every time.
Be done differently every time.
Not always include all items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be done the same way every time.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way each time. This helps you learn the steps and makes sure you don't forget anything.

questions.question: If you exit your vehicle improperly during the basic vehicle control skills test, you will:

options.text: Fail only that exercise.
Lose extra points on your score.
Automatically fail the entire test.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatically fail the entire test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the test, face the vehicle and always keep three points of contact. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: Texting while driving should:

options.text: Only be done on straight roads.
Only be done on curves.
Never be done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never be done.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and is not allowed at any time when operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: After you change a tire, you should:

options.text: Stop shortly after to check that the lug nuts are tight.
Repair the brakes.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop shortly after to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: Stop a short time after changing a tire to recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, you should:

options.text: Warm up the vehicle before driving to get fuel to the engine.
Let the air compressor reach at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
Start driving right after the vehicle starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the air compressor reach at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving, wait for the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. Watch the air pressure gauges.

questions.question: In a static leakage test, a triple combination vehicle with air brakes should lose no more than ____ in one minute.

options.text: 8 psi
5 psi
3 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: 5 psi
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle with air brakes should not lose more than 5 psi in one minute during a static leakage test. If air leaks faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must maintain ____ with the vehicle at all times.

options.text: Three points of contact
Four points of contact
Two points of contact

questions.correctAnswerText: Three points of contact
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic failure.

questions.question: If you must drive onto the shoulder in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Brake as hard as you can.
Get both sets of wheels onto the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.
questions.explanation: If you drive onto the shoulder to avoid a hazard, stay on it until you stop. Then signal, check your mirrors, and merge back into traffic. Avoid braking at speeds above 20 mph on the shoulder. Keep one set of wheels on the pavement if possible to maintain control.
